result.summary: OPERS’s February 2022 RFP seeks investment consulting services for its OPERS and URSJJ defined-benefit plans and SoonerSave and Pathfinder defined-contribution plans. It outlines proposal, qualification, assignment, timing, communication, fee, and reporting requirements, and reserves OPERS’s rights to reject, modify, negotiate, or make one or multiple awards; submissions become public records and proposal costs are not reimbursed. Vendors must submit the signed and notarized cover sheet and proposal through the designated file-drop portal by March 25, 2022, follow file and response instructions, disclose subcontracting, and meet applicable legal and fiduciary certifications. Questions were due March 11, with answers to be posted from March 16. The background identifies statutory authority, approximately $13 billion in defined-benefit assets and $1.6 billion in defined-contribution assets, the 14-member Board’s composition, OPERS’s authorized staffing and executive leadership, and introduces the plans’ asset-allocation targets.

THE OKLAHOMA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT SYSTEM
REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL
#515-22-200

nodes.title: INVESTMENT CONSULTING SERVICES
nodes.summary: OPERS is soliciting proposals from investment consulting firms to advise its two defined-benefit plans (OPERS and URSJJ) and two defined-contribution plans (SoonerSave and Pathfinder, each with 457 and 401(a) components). The RFP explains submission requirements; “Vendor” means any company, firm, or individual proposing. OPERS may reject any or all proposals, make no selection if none are satisfactory, modify the RFP before the deadline, and will not reimburse proposal costs. Submissions become OPERS property and are open to public inspection. The 11-section, 16-page RFP covers proposal forms and requirements, background, assignment scope, firm qualifications, timeline, communications, terms, questionnaire, fees, and sample reporting. It is available online or by email request. Vendors must follow submission instructions, reproduce the affidavit and questions exactly, and may not alter the RFP; alterations or misleading or false information may result in rejection or contract termination.

nodes.title: I. PROPOSAL COVER SHEET
nodes.summary: The proposal cover sheet for OPERS Investment Consulting Services RFP No. 515–22-200 (agency requisition 22-200), issued February 18, 2022, must be signed, notarized, and submitted with the original proposal by 4:30 p.m. CT on March 25, 2022. It requests vendor name, address, city/state/ZIP, telephone, and fax. The vendor affidavit requires a sworn representative to confirm authorization, personal knowledge of the proposal process, absence of collusion with vendors or state officials, and no payments or gifts offered for contract preference. The representative also certifies that proposal information is true and accurate. Signature/title, notary signature, date, seal, and commission-expiration fields are provided.

nodes.title: II. MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR SUBMITTING A PROPOSAL
nodes.summary: Proposals must be emailed through the specified OPERS file-drop portal by 4:30 p.m. Central, March 25, 2022; late or misdirected submissions are rejected. Include a completed, signed, notarized cover sheet; submit uncompressed PDF or DOC/DOCX files without external links. Timely proposals become OPERS property and, once opened, public records. Vendors consent to relevant records audits and are responsible for compliance, preparation, and any finalist presentation costs. Questions go by email to Lindsie Lundy by 5 p.m. Central, March 11; consolidated answers will be posted on OPERS’s website on or after March 16. OPERS may reject proposals, seek information or additional proposals, negotiate lower fees, and award all, part, none, or multiple contracts; consultant selection is exempt from competitive bidding. Proposals bind vendors, and submission accepts RFP terms. Vendors must not pay finder’s fees; acknowledge fiduciary duty, Oklahoma law, and incorporation of the RFP and response; answer in order and concisely, disclose subcontracting, and certify no Israel boycott when legally required. “Current” means June 30, 2021 unless stated otherwise.

nodes.title: A. Legal Authorization
nodes.summary: OPERS and URSJJ’s Board oversees about $13 billion in combined defined-benefit retirement funds and administers the SoonerSave and Pathfinder defined-contribution plans, which held about $1.6 billion total as of December 31, 2021. Investment authority and plan statutes are identified in Title 74 of the Oklahoma Statutes: Sections 909.1–909.2 for OPERS/URSJJ, Sections 1701 et seq. for SoonerSave, and Sections 935.1 et seq. for Pathfinder. OPERS has a 14-member Board comprising designated state officials and representatives, plus members appointed by the Governor (three), Supreme Court (one), House Speaker (two), and Senate President Pro Tempore (two). OPERS is authorized 63 staff, and its Executive Director is chief administrative officer. The text introduces the OPERS/URSJJ asset-allocation targets as of June 30, 2021, but provides no allocation figures.

result.title: TARGET MIXES FOR OPERS and URSJJ:
result.summary: The section sets OPERS/URSJJ target allocations at 34% large-cap domestic equities, 6% small-cap domestic equities, 28% international equities, 32% fixed income and 0% cash. It identifies custodial, recordkeeping, stable-value and investment-management providers and describes the plans’ investment options, shared options, unbundled structure and RFP-based provider selection; investment policies are available online. It outlines the consultant’s advisory, reporting, risk, compliance, manager-monitoring, provider-search, plan-option, ACFR and trustee-education duties, and minimum public-plan experience and staffing qualifications. It gives the procurement schedule and rules for vendor communications. General terms address Oklahoma law, vendor investigations and disclosures, continuity planning, assignment, renewal and termination, OPERS ownership of work, liability restrictions and fee parity. The questionnaire seeks firm, ownership, financial, staffing, client, investment-process, performance, conflict, fiduciary, reference, regulatory-registration and insurance information.

E. Investment Services Providers
The investment managers listed below manage the equities, cash, and fixed income portfolios for both OPERS and URSJJ. Although there are no investment manager searches planned during the next year, responding Vendors should anticipate that there could be one or more searches if needed.

nodes.title: Company Name
nodes.summary: The text lists Northern Trust as custodial bank and securities-lending provider; Empower Retirement as recordkeeper for SoonerSave and Pathfinder; and investment managers/providers for equity and fixed-income options: BlackRock, Westfield Capital, State Street Global Advisors, Newton, Barrow Hanley, DePrince Race & Zollo, UBS, Baillie Gifford, Mondrian, Hoisington, and TCW/Metropolitan West. Options include U.S. and international equity indices, large-cap growth and other large-cap equity, small-cap value and growth equity, international equity, constrained-core fixed income, TIPS index, interest-rate-anticipator fixed income, and core-plus fixed income. The plans use an unbundled arrangement, with Empower providing recordkeeping and fund options from various families; Great-West currently manages the Stable Value Fund. The OPERS Board selects each plan’s investment options under the Investment Policy. Options are shared between plans except those marked “(S),” which are SoonerSave-only.

Rowe Price Blue Chip, and TRP Total Equity Market Index (large-cap equity); Vanguard Select Value and Columbia Acorn Fund (subject to change) (mid-cap equity); Janus Henderson Small Cap Value and BlackRock Small Cap Growth (small-cap equity); American Funds EuroPacific Growth and TRP Emerging Markets Stock (international equity); Vanguard Target Retirement Income and 2020–2050 funds (target-date); BNY Mellon Small Cap Index (small-cap equity index); BNY Mellon ACWI ex-US Index (international equity index); and Vanguard Balanced Fund (balanced). System vendors, including investment managers, the master custodian, the defined-contribution recordkeeper, and the investment consultant, are competitively selected through RFPs. Except for the investment consulting RFP, the consultant is expected to work with staff on each RFP or search assignment.

nodes.title: F. Investment Guidelines
nodes.summary:
F. Investment Guidelines
A copy of the current “Statement of Policy” for OPERS and URSJJ, and the “Investment Policy and Guidelines” for both SoonerSave and Pathfinder are available on the OPERS website at https://www.opers.ok.gov/.

nodes.title: IV. SCOPE OF ASSIGNMENT
nodes.summary: The consultant advises on all investment activities for OPERS, URSJJ, SoonerSave and Pathfinder, coordinating with staff—primarily the CIO—to prepare and present materials for the Investment Committee and Board. Using custodian performance data, the consultant produces quarterly reports, presents defined-benefit plan reviews, helps reconcile results with managers and the custodian, and provides risk analytics. Duties also include monitoring Investment Policy compliance and recommending changes, reporting material developments affecting managers, and attending special meetings or researching additional topics. For searches of investment-related service providers, the consultant develops the RFP, evaluates responses and presents a documented report with chronology, methodology, exhibits and recommendations; site visits may be requested. The consultant annually reviews defined-contribution plan options and assists with replacements and provider selection, prepares investment sections for OPERS and URSJJ ACFRs, and every six years helps coordinate OPERS participation in the Oklahoma Public Fund Trustee Education Conference.

nodes.title: V. CRITERIA AND QUALIFICATIONS OF THE INVESTMENT CONSULTING FIRM
nodes.summary: Vendors must have substantial public defined benefit and defined contribution plan consulting experience, with no exceptions to the criteria: investment consulting must be a primary organizational business, including affiliates; the proposed consultant must have provided full-service consulting to at least five public pension plans with at least $1 billion in assets each as of June 30, 2021; and senior professionals must have at least ten years of institutional consulting experience. RFP fee quotes will significantly affect semifinalist selection. Investment guidelines for OPERS/URSJJ, SoonerSave, and Pathfinder are available on the OPERS website.

nodes.title: VII. COMMUNICATION WITH OPERS
nodes.summary: OPERS will answer RFP questions only through the process specified in Section II(G); vendors must check the website for updates, and telephone questions are not accepted. During the selection process, vendors may not contact OPERS Board members, consultants, or staff about the RFP, except through the designated Q&A process and with specified staff while they conduct negotiations, presentations, or contract award and execution. Normal business with OPERS’s incumbent investment consultant unrelated to the selection is permitted. Violations may result in proposal rejection. Vendors who submit proposals may not be notified of the Board’s final decision; announcing a preferred vendor, if any, may be OPERS’s only communication. Post-deadline telephone or other inquiries are discouraged.

nodes.title: VIII. GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS
key_items: A. Applicable Laws and Courts; B. Ethics in Public Contracting
D. Business Continuity; E. Assignment of Contract; F. Period of Contract; G. Ownership of Data and Work Product
G. Ownership of Data and Work Product
H. Limitation of Liability, Hold Harmless Clauses & Indemnity
nodes.summary: The solicitation and contract are governed by Oklahoma law, with litigation in Oklahoma County; vendors must follow applicable laws and certify their bids are free of collusion, fraud, kickbacks, and improper benefits to public employees. OPERS may investigate vendor qualifications, request information, visit offices, and reject unqualified proposals. Vendors must disclose corporate changes and provide a disaster business-continuity plan. Contracts cannot be assigned without OPERS’s written consent. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2022, with up to four annual renewals at the Board’s discretion; the Board may terminate on 30 days’ notice, with or without cause. Contract work product and compiled data belong to OPERS, which must have reasonable access. Oklahoma agencies cannot limit vendor liability, hold vendors harmless, or indemnify them. Investment consulting fees must match or undercut fees for comparable clients; vendors must report lower fees, reduce OPERS fees accordingly, and accept possible periodic reviews and retroactive reductions for failure to notify promptly.

nodes.title: IX. QUESTIONNAIRE
nodes.summary: The questionnaire requests information about the consulting firm’s identity, contacts, ownership and finances, services and revenue, organizational structure and changes, succession, litigation or investigations, staff compensation, five-year investment-professional staffing and turnover, proposed OPERS team biographies, account assignments and responsibilities, outside compensation, conflicts and their management. It asks whether the firm can meet the assignment scope and serve as fiduciary; client and plan profiles by type and size; firm-wide client gains, losses and assets; key professionals’ experience and time commitments; and investment philosophy, policy development, decision-making, capital-markets and manager research, active/passive views, selection and monitoring, watchlists, performance tracking, research priorities, strengths and weaknesses, portfolio-analysis systems, objectives and success measures, peer and manager universes, capital-market assumptions, guideline compliance, reporting customization and timing, and public-fund references. It also requests SEC registration and Form ADV information, plus errors-and-omissions and fiduciary-liability insurance coverage.

result.title: X. FEE QUOTE
result.summary: The RFP fee quote is a significant selection factor and must use the prescribed, unaltered fixed-fee format for all System assets. Bidding confirms acceptance of OPERS’ fee-calculation methodology; vendors are encouraged to obtain legal review. Quote the initial contract period (July 1, 2022–June 30, 2023) and annual fees for four years beginning on each July 1 contract anniversary. The fee must cover all investment consulting services, travel, and out-of-pocket expenses, and is the only fee OPERS will pay. Estimates may assume eight Board meetings and one Investment Manager Roundtable annually; four quarterly performance reports for OPERS and URSJJ with required analytics; periodic manager reports under the scope; at least two asset-allocation and liability studies, scheduled for May 2023 and May 2026; an annual DC-plan investment-options review; three special research projects over five years; and other scoped projects. State any additional assumptions. Provide total fees for the initial period and Years 1–4.
